newsitem.title: CHINA: China fines air firm for poor safety record.
newsitem.headline: China fines air firm for poor safety record.

text.p: The Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) imposed a fine of 500,000 yuan ($60,000) on a small domestic airline engaged in crop spraying for a poor safety record in 1996, officials and state media said on Friday.
The company based in Harbin, capital of northeastern Heilongjiang province, was engaged in industrial and agricultural flight and did not carry passengers, a CAAC official said by telephone.
Eight other air firms and their representatives were also punished for not meeting safety targets last year, the official said. He gave no further details.
At the end of last year, China's aviation sector had set a record of 29 months of safe flying, the Economic Information Daily said.
In 1994, the International Airline Passenger Association cited China as one of the most dangerous places in the world in which to fly, after a string of crashes and hijackings.
